From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Position Review (Buyer Side)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package shifts almost all known risk to the Buyer. It discloses the data room generally, excludes Buyer knowledge, shortens time limits, caps fundamental warranties, and leaves Riverlark debt, the Ironquay IP shortfall, bonuses and a possible privacy breach unresolved at Completion. Several Seller characterisations ("ordinary course", "not expected to be material", "settled") are not supported by the disclosed facts. The Buyer should not accept this package as a basis for mark-up.

**Limits of this review:** I have the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter, not the full draft SPA, so clause references are to the Seller's numbering. The disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so every open item needs a bring-down. NSW counsel should confirm the legal points below, particularly on fraud carve-outs, non-reliance and anti-sandbagging.

---

## A. Liability architecture

**1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% (AUD 4.8m)**
- The cap is a negotiable commercial term, but it is set alongside a warranty package that the Seller has largely neutralised through disclosure. A cap of 20% on a weakened warranty set is worth less than it appears.
- The Bluefen exposure alone (about AUD 3.6m revenue, roughly 30%) could generate losses that exceed the cap, so known issues must sit outside the general cap.
- **Push back:** Set the general cap at a higher level (commonly argued at 30–100% of price in Buyer mark-ups, depending on the deal). Exclude fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities from the cap. Make sure the cap is also not the Buyer's exclusive remedy for known issues.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k excess-only basket**
- An excess-only (deductible) basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of all warranty losses. Given that individual known items (Ironquay AUD 180k, bonuses AUD 420k) are close to or above that level, the deductible would absorb much of the recovery.
- **Push back:** Replace with a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar). Lower the de minimis, or remove it for related claims, and allow aggregation of claims arising from the same facts. Confirm whether de minimis claims count towards the basket. Exclude fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities from both thresholds.

**3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13): 18 months for general warranties; limitation applies to all Claims**
- 18 months is short for a business with unresolved IP, privacy and contractual issues. Those issues may take longer than 18 months to surface.
- Tax claims typically need to run until the ATO amendment period has expired, plus a buffer. The default limitation period for contract claims in NSW is six years, so the Seller's proposal is a significant cut-back.
- The proposal that any limitation applies to all Claims unless "expressly stated otherwise" would pull fundamental and tax claims into the 18-month window.
- **Push back:** General warranties at 24–36 months. Fundamental/title warranties at six years (or the statutory period). Tax claims until 60 days after the ATO amendment period for the relevant years expires. Specific indemnities to run until the relevant liability is resolved, with a reasonable long-stop. Reject the blanket "all Claims" limitation.

**4. Fundamental/title warranties subject to general caps and time limits**
- Title and capacity warranties are the core protection for what the Buyer is paying for. Subjecting them to a 20% cap and 18-month window is inconsistent with market practice and with the Buyer's basic risk position. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.
- **Push back:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price (or at least the purchase price), outside the basket and de minimis, with the longer time limit.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- This language would purport to cover fraud and claims based on the Seller's own misrepresentation. Under general principles, courts are unlikely to enforce a contractual exclusion of liability for the Seller's own fraud, and a clause of this breadth invites argument about enforceability. Misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18) may also be relevant depending on the claim. NSW counsel should confirm the wording.
- **Push back:** Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and fundamental warranties. Limit non-reliance to statements outside the SPA and make clear it does not apply to the warranties. Make the exclusive-remedy clause subject to specific indemnities and the price adjustment mechanism.

**6. Disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2)**
- Blanket disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records would defeat most of the Warranties. It would also make the Buyer responsible for finding and reading everything. This is the single most damaging provision in the package.
- **Push back:** Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Disclosure should be specific, fair, and made against identified warranties with reasonable particularity. Make clear that disclosure does not qualify specific indemnities or the price adjustment mechanism. Consider whether the Seller's "non-admission" language (DL 1.4) is acceptable, provided it is mutual and does not undermine the Buyer's claims.

**7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3)**
- The Seller wants the Buyer to be barred from claiming on anything known to it or its advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room. The Buyer has now read DD-002 to DD-012, so this clause would strip recovery on every issue in this letter, in combination with the general disclosure.
- The law on whether a buyer with actual knowledge can claim for breach is not settled and depends on wording. The Buyer should not leave this to argument.
- **Push back:** Express pro-sandbagging wording: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any knowledge, investigation or information. Delete the data-room deeming language.

---

## B. Known issues

**8. Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2): consent not obtained; reasonable endeavours and deemed satisfaction**
- Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. Change-control consent is outstanding, and conditions under clause 11.3 of the Bluefen contract are unverified.
- The Seller's proposal to use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent is weak. It does not address whether the consent is unconditional, whether conditions have been satisfied, or whether the consent is in the agreed form.
- **Push back:** Make Bluefen consent (unconditional or with conditions the Seller has satisfied, in agreed form) a condition precedent, not an endeavours obligation. Add a longstop date and a Buyer termination right. If consent is waived, add a price adjustment or escrow, and a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract or revenue, outside the cap and basket. Require the Seller to satisfy clause 11.3 conditions pre-Completion.

**9. Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3): AUD 3.2m debt; release "following Completion"**
- This is a clear error in a debt-free/cash-free deal. Debt must be repaid from the price at Completion, not after it. If the facility remains outstanding, the Buyer inherits both the debt and the security over the business while paying the full AUD 24m.
- Change-of-control clause 8.1 is also engaged, and discharge clause 9.2 is not satisfied.
- **Push back:** Require a payoff letter, repayment from the funds flow at Completion, discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations), release of any guarantees and confirmation that clause 8.1 does not trigger default post-Completion. The price should be reduced for any debt not repaid at Completion.

**10. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4): indemnity limited to SOW3; AUD 180k open**
- Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k appears open, with no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's view that the indemnity is "adequate" is not supported: the Buyer may not own the materials it is buying, and the indemnity is capped at a single payment.
- **Push back:** Require the Seller to pay the AUD 180k (or the Buyer deducts it from price) before Completion. Obtain a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Require a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP claims (not just SOW3), outside the cap and basket. Request the full SOW history and confirm no other open SOWs. Add an IP ownership warranty that is not subject to disclosure.

**11. Employee bonuses (DL 5): AUD 420k not in funds flow**
- The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller", but they are not reflected in the funds flow. Conditional bonuses payable on Completion are debt-like items; if the Buyer pays them post-Completion, it is funding the Seller's transaction cost.
- Payroll tax and superannuation on-costs are unaddressed. As an illustration (to be confirmed by the Buyer's payroll advisers): NSW payroll tax at 5.45% is roughly AUD 23k, and superannuation guarantee at 12% on bonuses that count as ordinary time earnings is roughly AUD 50k. Together, on-costs could be around AUD 73k.
- **Push back:** Treat the bonuses and all on-costs as debt-like items deducted from price, or require the Seller to fund them at or before Completion. Confirm the payment timing, the continued-employment conditions and whether any retention arrangements will continue post-Completion.

**12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Schedule 6; DL 6): ~1,240 records; "not expected to be material"**
- The records include names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. Even business contact details can be personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). If the incident is an eligible data breach (unauthorised access or disclosure likely to result in serious harm), the notifiable data breaches scheme applies: notification to the OAIC and affected individuals.
- The investigation is incomplete: access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. "Not expected to be material" has no stated basis, and the Seller cannot know this until the investigation is complete.
- **Push back:** Require a completed forensic investigation as a pre-Completion deliverable, with a remediation plan and any notifications made by the Seller before Completion. Add a specific privacy and cyber indemnity covering investigation, notification, remediation, third-party claims and regulatory costs (to the extent recoverable at law), outside the cap and basket. Consider a holdback or escrow sized to the investigation outcome. Warranty on privacy compliance and no unnotified breaches, not qualified by disclosure. Check whether W&I insurance (if used) will exclude this known matter.

**13. Office lease (cl 7; DL 7)**
- The lease has a notification obligation, and it is unclear whether a change of control requires landlord consent.
- **Push back:** Obtain the landlord's consent (or confirmation that none is required) and an estoppel certificate before Completion. Make it a condition precedent if the lease requires consent.

**14. Supplier renewals (DL 8): AUD 330k across three renewals of AUD 110k each**
- The three renewals appear to be related and are of equal value, which is consistent with splitting a larger commitment below a review threshold. Describing them as "ordinary course" is a characterisation, not evidence. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Push back:** Obtain the renewal contracts and any related correspondence. Treat any pre-Completion accrued portion as a debt-like item. Require the Seller to confirm termination rights. Add a warranty that no material contract has been renewed or varied outside the ordinary course.

**15. Mossvale (DL 9): assignment restriction**
- The disclosure does not confirm whether a share sale triggers consent. The Seller should not be able to rely on uncertainty.
- **Push back:** Require written confirmation from Mossvale that no consent is required, or obtain consent as a condition precedent.

---

## C. Title, tax and IP

**16. Title (DL 10; DD-012)**
- The share register identifies Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares. That is a starting point, not verification. The register is evidence of title, but the Buyer should verify it.
- **Push back:** Obtain ASIC current company extract, share certificates (if any), transfer forms, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation that no options or encumbrances exist, and a fundamental warranty of title with the protections in item 4.

**17. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
- That is not an acceptable position. Tax and IP risks are not adequately covered by general warranties with an 18-month window and a cap.
- **Push back:** Add a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering payroll tax, GST, PAYG and other pre-Completion liabilities), outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with the extended time limit. Add full tax warranties, a tax covenant and a conduct-of-tax-matters clause. Add IP ownership and non-infringement warranties not qualified by disclosure.

---

## D. Price mechanics (illustrative)

The funds flow should reflect a debt-free/cash-free adjustment. Items the Buyer should expect to deduct or see funded by the Seller:

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Repaid from price at Completion |
| Employee bonuses | 420,000 | Debt-like, deducted from price |
| Bonus on-costs (estimate) | ~73,000 | Debt-like, to be confirmed |
| Ironquay open balance | 180,000 | Paid by Seller or deducted |
| Supplier renewals (pre-Completion portion) | Up to 330,000 | Debt-like or Seller-funded, to be confirmed |
| **Identified total (excluding supplier portion)** | **~3,873,000** | |

The Bluefen revenue risk and any privacy liability are not included here and would require separate price protection, escrow or specific indemnity.

---

## E. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1 (must-have before any further negotiation):**
1. Delete general data room and public register disclosure (cl 1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7).
2. Delete the anti-sandbagging clause (cl 8.3) and insert express pro-sandbagging wording.
3. Carve out fraud and fundamental warranties from the non-reliance, limitation and exclusive-remedy provisions (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
4. Move fundamental and tax warranties outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with longer time limits.
5. Correct the Riverlark treatment: repay from price at Completion with discharge of security.
6. Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent, with a longstop and termination right.

**Priority 2 (key commercial protections):**
7. Raise the general cap and replace the deductible basket with a tipping basket; lower or remove the de minimis.
8. Extend general warranty time limits to 24–36 months; tax to the ATO period plus buffer.
9. Specific indemnities (outside cap and basket) for Ironquay IP, the privacy incident and Bluefen.
10. Treat bonuses, on-costs, the Ironquay balance and pre-Completion supplier amounts as debt-like or Seller-funded.
11. Require completed privacy investigation and any notifications pre-Completion; consider holdback or escrow.

**Priority 3 (verification and conditions):**
12. Obtain the landlord consent or estoppel (lease) and Mossvale confirmation.
13. Obtain the Ironquay confirmatory IP assignment and full SOW history.
14. Verify title independently (ASIC extract, PPSR search, transfer documents).
15. Obtain the supplier renewal contracts and confirm termination rights.
16. Require a full bring-down of all DD items, since the disclosure is dated 22 September 2026.

**Overall position:** Reject the "fair and balanced" framing. The package allocates known risks to the Buyer, uses disclosure and knowledge rules to remove the Buyer's protections, and leaves material debt and IP issues unresolved at Completion. The Buyer's mark-up should lead with items 1–6 above and make clear that the price and Completion mechanics cannot proceed until the Riverlark, Bluefen and Ironquay items are resolved.

- The investigation is incomplete: access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. "Not expected to be material" has no stated basis, and the Seller cannot know this until the investigation is complete.
- **Push back:** Require a completed forensic investigation as a pre-Completion deliverable, with a remediation plan and any notifications made by the Seller before Completion. Add a specific privacy and cyber indemnity covering investigation, notification, remediation, third-party claims and regulatory costs (to the extent recoverable at law), outside the cap and basket. Consider a holdback or escrow sized to the investigation outcome. Warranty on privacy compliance and no unnotified breaches, not qualified by disclosure. Check whether W&I insurance (if used) will exclude this known matter.

**13. Office lease (cl 7; DL 7)**
- The lease has a notification obligation, and it is unclear whether a change of control requires landlord consent.
- **Push back:** Obtain the landlord's consent (or confirmation that none is required) and an estoppel certificate before Completion. Make it a condition precedent if the lease requires consent.

**14. Supplier renewals (DL 8): AUD 330k across three renewals of AUD 110k each**
- The three renewals appear to be related and are of equal value, which is consistent with splitting a larger commitment below a review threshold. Describing them as "ordinary course" is a characterisation, not evidence. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Push back:** Obtain the renewal contracts and any related correspondence. Treat any pre-Completion accrued portion as a debt-like item. Require the Seller to confirm termination rights. Add a warranty that no material contract has been renewed or varied outside the ordinary course.

**15. Mossvale (DL 9): assignment restriction**
- The disclosure does not confirm whether a share sale triggers consent. The Seller should not be able to rely on uncertainty.
- **Push back:** Require written confirmation from Mossvale that no consent is required, or obtain consent as a condition precedent.

## C. Title, tax and IP

**16. Title (DL 10; DD-012)**
- The share register identifies Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares. That is a starting point, not verification. The register is evidence of title, but the Buyer should verify it.
- **Push back:** Obtain ASIC current company extract, share certificates (if any), transfer forms, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation that no options or encumbrances exist, and a fundamental warranty of title with the protections in item 4.

**17. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
- That is not an acceptable position. Tax and IP risks are not adequately covered by general warranties with an 18-month window and a cap.
- **Push back:** Add a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering payroll tax, GST, PAYG and other pre-Completion liabilities), outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with the extended time limit. Add full tax warranties, a tax covenant and a conduct-of-tax-matters clause. Add IP ownership and non-infringement warranties not qualified by disclosure.

## E. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1 (must-have before any further negotiation):**
1. Delete general data room and public register disclosure (cl 1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7).
2. Delete the anti-sandbagging clause (cl 8.3) and insert express pro-sandbagging wording.
3. Carve out fraud and fundamental warranties from the non-reliance, limitation and exclusive-remedy provisions (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
4. Move fundamental and tax warranties outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with longer time limits.
5. Correct the Riverlark treatment: repay from price at Completion with discharge of security.
6. Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent, with a longstop and termination right.

**Priority 2 (key commercial protections):**
7. Raise the general cap and replace the deductible basket with a tipping basket; lower or remove the de minimis.
8. Extend general warranty time limits to 24–36 months; tax to the ATO period plus buffer.
9. Specific indemnities (outside cap and basket) for Ironquay IP, the privacy incident and Bluefen.
10. Treat bonuses, on-costs, the Ironquay balance and pre-Completion supplier amounts as debt-like or Seller-funded.
11. Require completed privacy investigation and any notifications pre-Completion; consider holdback or escrow.

**Priority 3 (verification and conditions):**
12. Obtain the landlord consent or estoppel (lease) and Mossvale confirmation.
13. Obtain the Ironquay confirmatory IP assignment and full SOW history.
14. Verify title independently (ASIC extract, PPSR search, transfer documents).
15. Obtain the supplier renewal contracts and confirm termination rights.
16. Require a full bring-down of all DD items, since the disclosure is dated 22 September 2026.

**Overall position:** Reject the "fair and balanced" framing. The package allocates known risks to the Buyer, uses disclosure and knowledge rules to remove the Buyer's protections, and leaves material debt and IP issues unresolved at Completion. The Buyer's mark-up should lead with items 1–6 above and make clear that the price and Completion mechanics cannot proceed until the Riverlark, Bluefen and Ironquay items are resolved.
